gate.consequence_fired: the integration layer does not recover the specialist gains: late fusion and/or competence routing lose to the single global arm or to identity routing; M143 closes as a scoped negative and the interface itself is the finding.
gate.consequence_passed: the integration layer recovers the specialist gains: late fusion beats the global arm on held-out rows and competence routing beats identity routing, which beats the random router; the integration layer is promoted to the v22 system design.
gate.registered: fired if fused < global - 0.005 on the eval half, OR competence < identity, OR identity < random; all measured on the eval half of the sealed test rows.

phase2.note: penalty selected on a validation slice (first 80% of the seeded fit-half permutation) by valid accuracy; refit on the whole fit half; evaluated on the eval half only.

config.question: E10 sealed that hard routing loses (routed 18.8% / oracle 20.5% < global 22.5%). Does the integration layer - one closed-form fit over the concatenated scores of the six specialists plus the global model (late fusion), and a router trained to predict WHICH arm is right (competence routing) - recover the specialist gains that hard routing lost?

registration_notes.N97.1: Phase 1 recomputes the six per-domain specialist score matrices (512-atom A5 dictionaries, the exact M139b construction) plus the global head and domain router from the sealed f6144 codes, and caches the score matrices under data_cache_root()/v16/m143/scores.npz. No sealed evidence is modified.
registration_notes.N97.2: t1 anchors in phase 1: class head reproduces 0.22487 (tol 0.002); domain router reproduces 0.7559 (tol 0.002); each specialist's own-domain accuracy reproduces the M119 sealed curve value (tol 0.002).
registration_notes.N97.3: Phase 2 uses a deterministic 50/50 split of the sealed test rows (seed 33). The FIT half fits the stacking head (ridge over the 7x345 concatenated scores) and the competence router (ridge 2415 -> 7 arms; AMENDED 14 Aug after the inadmissible smoke: the target is the lowest-index arm whose argmax matches the row label - the plan's own wording 'predict which model will be correct' - labels on the fit half only; the original score-derived target was broken because raw-score magnitudes are not comparable across arms). The EVAL half measures everything.
registration_notes.N97.3b: AMENDED 14 Aug after the inadmissible smoke: the penalty ladder is {1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000} (was {1,10,100,1000}); at the wide-design operating point (2415 features, ~800 smoke fit rows) the optimum sat above 1000 (smoke ladder scores peaked at the top). Registered before the full run.
registration_notes.N97.4: The stacking guarantee (fused >= any single arm) holds on the FIT half by construction; the registered question is whether it survives to the EVAL half.
registration_notes.N97.5: Gate (kill switch): fired if fused < global - 0.005 on the eval half, OR competence < identity, OR identity < random (all measured on the eval half). Random router = expectation over 10 seeded draws.
registration_notes.N97.6: Smoke runs declare _smoke_note and MUST refuse the sealed output directory; smoke caps rows and skips no gates except inadmissibility.
registration_notes.N97.7: Dated snapshot; all seeds, penalties and the split registered for byte-repeat.

sealed_codes.note: Global fallback + domain router fitted on the SEALED 6144-atom memmaps (dual accumulate, the M139a convention).

sparse.specialist_construction: A5-exact (M119/M124/M139b): global M108 whitener; per-domain candidate pool (n_cap 20000, seed [11, domain]) restricted to the domain's train rows; dictionary = candidates in the [11,100] seeded-permutation order, first 512 atoms; triangle encode on GPU with the registered throttle; closed-form ridge lambda=1.0.
